messages:
tara: Heads up — our latest image scan flagged two high-ish vulns hitting alpine-minimal: CVE-2026-1401 (OpenSSL) and CVE-2026-1402 (glibc). image sha: abc123. @sam can you triage blast radius?

sam: On it. I'll enumerate images that inherit alpine-minimal and surface which services are at risk. quick thought: most runtime images use it, infra tools maybe too.

lee: Do we know arch impact? x86 + arm64? we ship multiarch.

registry-bot: scan report: repo/redwood/runtime:alpine-minimal@sha256:abc123 -> 12 vulnerabilities (2 HIGH: CVE-2026-1401, CVE-2026-1402). Full report uploaded to S3: https://s3.redwood.internal/scans/1887654321-report.json

maria: If we rebuild we must re-run signing and SLSA attestation. Also need audit log entries for KMS usage. I'll handle signing policy changes, but we need an approval window.

sam: Proposed plan (short):
1) patch Dockerfile to pick updated libssl/libc packages
2) rebuild multiarch images in ephemeral runners
3) run smoke + e2e canary in staging for 2 hours
4) sign images with KMS key and push to registry
5) promote to prod if canary green
ETA for canary start: tomorrow 09:00 UTC unless objections.

tara: Add RBAC step: require explicit image-signer role to call KMS key. @maria please confirm the IAM role and audit trail. @oncall please approve tomorrow 09:00-11:00 UTC window.

oncall: Approved for 09:00-11:00 UTC. I will monitor alerts and paging during canary.

lee: Will run compat tests for musl vs glibc behavior — remember prior arm64 glibc mixing caused SIGSEGV in worker. Quick local test command:

```sh
# rebuild snippet (local)
docker build -t repo/redwood/runtime:alpine-minimal-patch-2026 -f Dockerfile.alpine .
# verify openssl version inside the image
docker run --rm repo/redwood/runtime:alpine-minimal-patch-2026 openssl version -a
# run unit smoke tests
docker run --rm repo/redwood/runtime:alpine-minimal-patch-2026 pytest -q tests/smoke || exit 1
```

sam: We'll gate promotion on: image-scan clean (no high), signed image present, canary error rate <0.1% and no regression alerts. Also will update deployment manifests with new image checksum and add a presubmit check for signed images.

security-bot: Policy trigger: production tags require signed images. Current prod tag 'v2026-02' unsigned -> automated block until signed image is available.

maria: KMS note: use key id 'redwood-build-key-2024'. I'll open a PR to add iam:PassRole for the 'image-signer' service account and add audit annotations for each signing operation. Also will add a short runbook entry for key rotation impacts.

tara: If canary shows any of the following we rollback immediately and open incident: error rate >=0.5%, p50/p95 latency spike >2x, or core dumps. Rollback plan: retag previous image as prod and trigger rolling deploy; notify customers.

sam: I'll create the patch branch + PR today and include the rebuild workflow. Will also request ephemeral build capacity from infra.

lee: Reminder: test arm64 on Graviton/AMD too. We've had platform-specific crypto quirks before.

oncall: I'll post the canary watch doc to #eng-oncall an hour before start and enable extended logging for the canary nodes.

tara: Thanks. I'll update security/runbook.md with the triage notes and make a compliance ticket for the signed artifact evidence. :thumbsup:

maria: PR for IAM + signing policy opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/4123 — review appreciated.

sam: Leaving a quick checklist in the PR: rebuild, scan, compat tests, sign, push, canary, promote. I'll ping once CI artifacts are ready.

registry-bot: Reminder: push-time attestation required. Please ensure cosign/SLSA step completes before promotion.

tara: Great. Closing loop here — we'll reconvene after the canary. If anything unexpected shows up, escalate in #incidents.
